fields.question: What is encapsulation in OOP?
fields.answer: Encapsulation means bundling data and methods that operate on that data inside a class, and restricting direct access to some of the object's components.

fields.question: What is the difference between composition and inheritance?
fields.answer: Inheritance models an is-a relationship by extending a base class. Composition models a has-a relationship by storing other objects as fields. Composition is often preferred for flexibility and looser coupling.

fields.question: What is the role of Django migrations?
fields.answer: Migrations are versioned schema changes derived from models. They let you apply, reverse, and share database structure updates across environments with migrate.

fields.question: Why use AUTH_USER_MODEL instead of django.contrib.auth.models.User?
fields.answer: AUTH_USER_MODEL lets you swap in a custom user early so ForeignKeys point to your model. Changing the user model after tables exist is painful, so set it before the first migrate.

fields.question: What is the difference between 1:N and N:M relationships?
fields.answer: 1:N means one parent row links to many child rows via a ForeignKey. N:M means each side can link to many of the other, usually through an intermediate table.

fields.question: What is a database index and when would you add one?
fields.answer: An index is a data structure that speeds up lookups at the cost of write overhead and storage. Add indexes for frequent filters and joins, especially on foreign keys and search columns.

fields.question: What is a prompt in an LLM application?
fields.answer: A prompt is the input text (and structure) you send to the model: instructions, context, and the user question. Prompt quality strongly affects output quality.

fields.question: What are tokens and why do they matter for cost and limits?
fields.answer: Tokens are chunks of text the model reads and generates. API pricing and context windows are measured in tokens, so longer prompts and answers cost more and may hit limits.

fields.question: What is RAG in simple terms?
fields.answer: RAG retrieves relevant documents from your data store, then inserts them into the prompt so the LLM answers with grounded context instead of relying only on its training memory.

fields.question: Why do we chunk documents before embedding them for RAG?
fields.answer: Chunking keeps retrieved context within size limits, improves retrieval precision, and reduces noise. Too-large chunks dilute relevance; too-small chunks lose meaning.
